misreading: All four read the template "T skip ID dependency" as having a placeholder for the blocking dependency's ID and emit e.g. "5 skip b a" instead of the literal word "5 skip b dependency" (they even disagree on which dep ID: F3 min ID, others first-in-list). F3 additionally cannot preempt for a tag conflict when a slot is free (R42).
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: No visible test involves a terminal failure that blocks a dependent job, so no skip line is ever produced.
prevention: In output templates, treat lowercase words as literal text and only UPPERCASE tokens as placeholders; reproduce templates verbatim, never substituting plausible data.

misreading: The next-tick computation includes the running customer's work_at only while arrivals remain; the arm (None, Some(finish)) jumps straight to finish, so once arrivals are exhausted the protection-end tick is skipped and a superior waiter that arrived during switching never preempts at work_at.
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: The only switching-cost test has no superior waiter pending at work_at, so skipping that tick yields the same trace.
prevention: In discrete-event loops, compute the next time as the minimum over every event source in every branch; test the case where one source is exhausted.

misreading: Encoder::current_column is a stub returning 0 and set_current_column is a no-op, so Wrapped streaming encoding restarts each push/finish at column 0 and omits row separators across chunk boundaries; chunked output differs from one-shot encode.
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: Visible tests never exercise Wrapped encoding (streaming or one-shot); the encoder chunk test uses Whitespace::None.
prevention: For streaming APIs, persist all formatting state across calls, leave no stub helpers, and verify chunked output equals one-shot output for every option combination.

misreading: decode_many preallocates Vec::with_capacity(count) from the caller-supplied count, so a huge count (e.g. usize::MAX) panics with capacity overflow (or aborts on allocation) instead of returning the Truncated error from the first missing integer.
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: Visible tests only use count 0 and 2, where preallocation is harmless.
prevention: Never preallocate from caller-supplied counts or sizes; grow incrementally or cap capacity by what the input can actually supply, so extreme values cannot panic.

misreading: The DP only allows a marker-ended line whose sole content is a prefix of the line's starting word, never completed word(s) followed by a hyphenated prefix of the next word (e.g. "aa bb~cc" width 6 should be ["aa bb-","cc"], it yields ["aa","bbcc"]); it also omits R23's +3 single-piece penalty on marker-only and raw-split lines.
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: The only hyphen test has a single word, where a marker prefix is necessarily alone on its line and is the only legal layout, so neither omission changes output.
prevention: Derive legal moves from all rules combined (e.g., items followed by a split) and apply every cost term to each move type.
